statement: Let $f(x)=\dfrac{x+2}{x}$. Find a simplified expression for $f(f(x))$ and determine the fixed points of $f$ (values of $x$ with $f(x)=x$).
solution: $f(f(x))=f\!\left(\dfrac{x+2}{x}\right)=\dfrac{\frac{x+2}{x}+2}{\frac{x+2}{x}} =1+\dfrac{2x}{x+2}=\dfrac{x+2+2x}{x+2}=\dfrac{3x+2}{x+2}$. Fixed points satisfy $\dfrac{x+2}{x}=x$, i.e. $x^{2}=x+2$, so $x^{2}-x-2=0$ and $(x-2)(x+1)=0$. The fixed points are $x=2$ and $x=-1$.
hints: Compose $f$ with itself and simplify the complex fraction.
Set $f(x)=x$ and solve the resulting quadratic.
